explanation: Matches erdosproblems.com/695, first question: for primes p_1 < p_2 < ⋯ with p_{i+1} ≡ 1 (mod p_i), is lim p_k^{1/k} = ∞? The Lean statement: for every strictly increasing sequence of primes q with q(i+1) mod q(i) = 1, q(k)^{1/k} → ∞. The 0-based indexing changes the exponent from 1/(k+1) to 1/k, which does not affect divergence ((q^{1/k})^{k/(k+1)} → ∞ iff q^{1/k} → ∞). Faithful (positive form of the yes/no question).
